full_judgment:
2. Facts, for disposal of the appeal in short are that the predecessor of respondent No.1 to 9 late Mahbub Rahim Chowdhury and others filed Other Suit No. 20 of 1991 for declaration of their title and confirmation of possession in the suit land contending, inter-alia, that by kabala dated 9-1-1915 Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury purchased 40 decimals of land, but though the kabala was registered in the name of Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury he was only two annas share holder of that land and the remaining 14 annas share of that purchased land belonged to his other co-sharers. Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury died in 1937 leaving behind wife Asia Khatun along with one son Mahbub Rahim Chowdhury and one daughter Salima Khatun as his heirs. Subsequently, Asia Khatun died in 1967. That the son and daughter of late Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury had been enjoying and possessing two annas share in the suit land and the other co-sharers had been enjoying and possessing rest 14 annas share of the suit land in ejmali. That the said son and daughters of Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury by executing a registered Muktinama dated 18-12-1975 admitted that their predecessor Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury was benamder in respect of 14 annas share in the suit land. In 1938 a hat was started in the suit land. Subsequently 22 decimals of land out of that 40 decimals of land was acquired by the Government and in that acquired 22 decimals of land the hat named as 'Cornal Hat' was started. That Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury and his other co-sharers established the Cornal Hat High School in the suit land in the year 1909 and subsequently in the year 1941 the said school was renamed as Cornal Hat Nurul Hoque Chowdhury High School. That the rent realized for 22 decimals of land was paid to the said school and after acquisition of said 22 decimals of land by the government the compensation also was paid to the said school. The plaintiff by constructing several huts in the suit land leased out those to monthly tenants and have been enjoying and possessing the suit land through those monthly tenants. That the plaintiffs or their predecessor never transferred the suit land to the said school or to anybody else. But the PS Khatin of the suit land was wrongly prepared in the name of the defendants though the defendants have got no right and title in the suit land, rather they are mere monthly evictable tenants under the plaintiffs. The suit land was never donated by the plaintiffs or their predecessor to the school by executing any deed or orally. 

 3. The defendant Nos.1, 16 to 21, 57 and 58 contested that suit by filing written statements. The materials case of the contesting defendant No.1 was that Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury was the original owner of the suit land and in 1937 he orally donated the suit land to Cornal Hat High School and handed over possession also. The said school was subsequently renamed as Cornal Hat Nurul Hoque Chowdhury High School. That the said school settled 6 decimals of land out of the suit land to the father of the defendant No.1 and one decimal of land to the defendant No.1. The defendant No.1 and his father used to pay rent to the said school. They also constructed shops in their said lands and leased out those to different monthly tenants. After the death of his father the defendant No.1 and his brothers and sisters inherited that 6 decimals of land settled with their father. The other brothers and sisters of the defendant No.1 sold their shares to the defendant No.1 and thus the defendant No.1 became the owner of entire 7 decimals of land settled to him and to his father by the school and has also been enjoying and possessing the same. That the plaintiffs have got no right, title and possession in the suit land. 

 4. The defendant Nos.16-19 contested the suit by filing another set of written statement stating that the suit land belonged to Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury who donated the suit land to Kattully High English School and subsequently the said school settled the suit land with one Ruhul Amin. The father of these defendants purchased the suit land from the said Ruhul Amin and became owner and possessor of the said land. After the death of their father these defendants have been enjoying and possessing the suit land. The PS record in respect of the suit land was prepared in the name of their father. The defendants have been enjoying and possessing the suit land by paying rent to the government. 

 5. The defendant No.2 filed another written statement stating that the suit land belonged to Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury who orally donated the suit land to Comal Hat High English School. The said School settled the suit land with different persons who have been enjoying and possessing the suit land by constructing different shops thereon. After acquisition of the suit land by the government compensation was paid to the said school. That the father of this defendant took settlement of the suit land from the said school and after the death of his father this defendant has been enjoying and possessing the suit land as tenant under the government on payment of rent to the government. 

 6. The defendant Nos.57 and 58 contested the suit by filing another set of written statement stating that the suit land belonged to Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury who donated the same orally to the Cornal Hat High English School. That the said school settled the suit land with their father and their father paid the rent of the suit land to the school and since after acquisition of the suit land by the government their father had been paying rent to the government. After the death of their father the defendant Nos.57 and 58 have become the owners of the suit land and they have been also possessing the same. The PS Khatian of the suit land was prepared in the name of their father. 

 10. Mr Aj Mohammad Ali, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the appellants mainly contending the grounds of the leave granting order emphatically argues that the trial court on proper consideration of the materials on records dismissed the suit with the findings that the suit suffers from defect of parties and the plaintiffs are not entitled to get the decree since they failed to prove their right, title and possession over the suit land, rather the suit land was orally donated by late Nozir Ahmed Chowdhury to the school and the school settled the suit land to the predecessors of the defendants and predecessors of the defendants are tenants under the school and after enactment of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act they became tenants under the government and now the defendants have been enjoying and possessing the suit land having their legal right, title and possession over the same on payment of rents to the government, but the appellate Court as the last court of fact without properly reversing those findings illegally set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and finally decreed the suit which has occasioned failure of justice. 

 11. He further submits that the appellate court arrived at its decision in an illegal manner without finding that the school took compensation for acquisition of the suit land from the government and the predecessors of the defendants were tenants under the school. The appellate court also failed to consider the presumptive value of the recent records of right which were prepared in the names of the predecessors of the defendants. As per him the appellate court committed illegality in not finding that the suit suffers from defect of parties and, as such, it is not maintainable. He submits that under the facts and circumstances of the present case the plaintiff was under obligation legally to add the government as necessary party in the suit mandatorily. On this point he has referred President Order No. 142 of 1972.
